source.title: Domain Restriction via Multi SAE Layer Transitions

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses pretrained SAEs as a representation tool for OOD detection and motivates them by superposition, but does not test the claim versions about superposition, polysemanticity, or SAE features as canonical model units.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses superposition and applies SAEs, but its experiments target domain/OOD detection rather than whether features overlap as nearly orthogonal directions, how feature sparsity or importance affects geometry, or whether SAEs recover complete and stable model units. OOD detection scores and backend comparisons are results of the paper's own method, not measurements of the claim. Figure 2's feature-overlap analysis is recorded as a related finding, not as evidence for a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper uses pretrained Gemma Scope-style 16k SAEs as a fixed representation for ID-only OOD detection. It cites superposition as motivation. Its results are its own method's AUROC/AUPR/FPR and SAE feature-overlap statistics, so none bears on whether superposition, polysemanticity or SAE feature canonicality holds. The raw-activation ablation (AUROC 0.753 vs ~0.92 with SAE) is a method-performance comparison that the authors attribute to superposition only speculatively; it does not measure superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that depthwise SAE feature transitions give a strong ID-only scope-gating signal, especially far-OOD and several near-OOD settings. Discrimination degrades when task taxonomy is finer-grained than SAE feature resolution (CLINC150, Gemma2-2B). They speculate that the poor raw-activation results reflect superposition, but do not test this.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses pretrained SAEs and sequential anomaly scorers for OOD detection; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.method_sensitivity: The feature-overlap profile is examined across layers and Top-k settings; the paper reports a top-k sweep for OOD detection, but those results do not test the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma2-2B, mean Jaccard similarity of top-k SAE features among in-domain inputs is low in early layers, peaks mid-depth, and declines in late layers (Figure 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-consistent SAE features in LLMs are most shared across inputs in middle layers.

record.code_released: no; the paper says code will be released in the future
record.problems: The paper does not directly test superposition or SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonicality. Its representation analysis is limited to SAE feature-set overlap across depth, and the experiments use SAE-16k; the authors note that evaluating more expressive SAEs such as 65k is future work.
record.rows_left_out: OOD detection metrics, backend comparisons, and the raw-activation ablation were omitted because they report performance of the paper's own scope-gating method, not outcomes that measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy models; no measurement of overlapping near-orthogonal directions, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated vs shared dimensions.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
SAEs are applied, but there is no test of whether they recover the model's sparse features. The raw-vs-SAE OOD ablation is method performance only.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicality. Only a 16k SAE is used; the CLINC150 'resolution mismatch' is an interpretation, not measured.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification is confirmed. The study is a preprint and code is not released.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-model test or measurement of overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemantic neurons.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
The paper applies pretrained SAEs but does not test whether they recover sparse model features or whether features are spread across neurons.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean Jaccard similarity of top-k SAE feature sets for pairs of in-domain inputs across layers.

conditions.value: all pairs from a subset of 1000 in-domain samples

rows.measure: Mean Jaccard similarity of active SAE feature sets
rows.note: The text describes lower feature agreement in early layers, greater similarity in mid-layers, and more input-specific features in late layers. This is a depthwise feature-overlap result, not a measurement of superposition geometry or SAE recovery.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. Within-domain Jaccard overlap of top-k SAE features across layers is a domain-consistency diagnostic, not a measure of superposition geometry, SAE recovery, or feature completeness/stability. The value is figure-only with no baseline.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
